samples.summary: New `mergeInlineStyle` helper in block-helpers has no direct unit test, and the existing `applyInlineStyle` tests there cannot detect the behavior it adds
samples.evidence: `mergeInlineStyle` (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:316) is the new merge that deletes keys whose patch value is `undefined`. The dedicated suite `packages/docs/test/store/block-helpers.test.ts` `describe('applyInlineStyle')` (lines 183-227) never applies a patch containing an `undefined` value, and all its assertions use `toEqual({ text, style })`, which treats `{bold: undefined}` and `{}` as equal — so even if the delete loop were removed those tests stay green. The only coverage of the delete is indirect, via the heading-6 test in document.test.ts (`'bold' in (cd?.style ?? {})`).

samples.summary: The stated motivation of the change — a cleared run follows a named style that is later redefined to set the flag — is never asserted by any test
samples.evidence: The `styleOffAsClear` doc comment (document.ts:387-392) justifies the change by the lazy-cascade hazard: a stored `false` pins the run against a style later redefined to set the key. The added tests only assert run re-merge and key absence; no test redefines a style in `_document.styles` after a toggle-off and asserts the run now resolves with the flag on. I grepped the docs test tree for style-redefinition + toggle-off combinations and found none.

samples.summary: Pending-style flush path (typing after a toggle-off at a collapsed caret), explicitly named in the task scope, has no test asserting the flag is now cleared rather than stored as `false`
samples.evidence: `pending.consumeForInsert` routes through `doc.applyInlineStyle` (pending-style.ts:34), so it is affected by `styleOffAsClear`, and docs/tasks/active/20260819-docs-inline-style-off-clears-key-todo.md:35 lists 'the pending-style flush' as covered by the fix. I found no test that toggles a boolean off at a collapsed caret, types, and asserts the typed run lacks the key (searched packages/docs/test for 'pending').

samples.summary: The deliberate exclusions from BOOLEAN_INLINE_STYLE_KEYS (notably `pageNumber`, and all non-boolean keys) are undocumented by any test
samples.evidence: The comment at document.ts:31-34 says `pageNumber` is intentionally excluded because it is structural. No test asserts that `{pageNumber: false}` (or any non-listed key set to `false`) is still passed through unchanged; a future contributor deriving the list from `InlineStyle` would break the intent with no failing test. Searched packages/docs/test for 'pageNumber' toggle-off assertions.

samples.summary: The named-style exception is only exercised via the built-in heading-6 italic; no test covers a user override in `_document.styles`, nor the exception inside a table cell / header block, nor the cell-rectangle write
samples.evidence: `styleOffAsClear` resolves defaults via `resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), this._document.styles)` — the second argument (the document's override registry) is never non-empty in any test, and `findBlock` also reaches header/footer/cell blocks (document.ts:176-186) but the exception is tested only on a top-level heading paragraph. `applyInlineStyleToCells` is tested for the clearing branch only (backward-selection-toggle.test.ts:636), never for the keep-`false` branch.

samples.summary: The `'italic' in style` / `key in style` assertions in the two re-merge tests are non-discriminating; only the `toHaveLength(1)` assertion carries the coverage
samples.evidence: `normalizeInlines` (block-helpers.ts:80-84) keeps the *first* matching run's style object when merging, so after the runs re-merge the surviving style is the untouched neighbour's `{}` — `'italic' in inlines[0].style` is false whether or not `mergeInlineStyle` deletes the key. Same for the loop test at lines 325-341. Not vacuous overall (the length assertion does fail without the fix), but the `in` assertions imply coverage of the key-delete that they do not provide.
